He was stabbed by his co-pilot but continued fighting, helping prevent what Israeli officials believe was an attempt to crash a passenger jet carrying mostly Israelis: Indian pilot Smit Machchhar has emerged as one of the central figures in the drama aboard Flydubai Flight FZ1073.
Machchhar, the captain of the aircraft diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, was wounded during the struggle with the Omani co-pilot suspected of trying to bring down the plane.
He was identified in India and Israel as the captain involved in the incident. According to his LinkedIn profile, Machchhar has about 15 years of experience flying for commercial airlines.
He joined the Emirati carrier Flydubai in June 2022 after spending 11 years with Indian low-cost airline SpiceJet.
According to his profile, Machchhar had logged more than 9,750 flight hours on Boeing 737 aircraft, including the 737-800 and Boeing 737 MAX 8 and 9. His current total is likely higher.
During his years at SpiceJet, he accumulated more than 9,500 flight hours, including over 6,400 hours as pilot in command.
Machchhar also served as a training captain, instructing, mentoring and evaluating other pilots.
The experience became critical Wednesday morning when the routine Dubai-Tel Aviv flight turned into a cockpit emergency.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said later that “during the flight, as they approached Israel, one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot and apparently tried to crash the plane with everyone aboard.”
Netanyahu said he had spoken with one of the Israeli passengers involved in stopping the suspected attacker.
“He told me that the plane entered a spin and began to plunge,” Netanyahu said. “He told me that, somehow, he managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members, and together they subdued the stabbing pilot while he was trying to sabotage the aircraft’s systems.”
Two additional pilots then entered the cockpit and took control of the aircraft, whose tail was damaged during the rapid descent.
One of the passengers who helped restrain the suspected attacker said a doctor then assisted the wounded captain.
“We neutralized him, the terrorist, and a doctor helped the chief pilot and stabilized him,” the passenger said. “It was insane.”
Passengers said they restrained the suspected attacker using cables from the multimedia headphones distributed aboard the flight.
After the aircraft made its emergency landing in Tabuk, the passengers remained in Saudi Arabia for several hours before boarding another Flydubai aircraft for Israel.
They landed at Ben Gurion Airport Wednesday evening, bringing an end to a journey that began as a routine flight from Dubai and became a violent struggle inside the cockpit.

Volkswagen, Chinese battery-maker Gotion plan $3.66B battery investment in Europe, North Africa
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

Mucahithan Avcioglu
30 September 2026•Update: 30 September 2026
Volkswagen and Chinese battery maker Gotion High-tech plan to invest €3.22 billion ($3.66 billion) in battery and materials production projects in Europe and North Africa to develop a regional supply chain for the European market.
The plan involves three joint ventures in Valencia, Spain; Surany, Slovakia; and Kenitra, Morocco, according to Gotion’s investment announcement and a Volkswagen statement released Monday. Gotion’s contribution totals approximately €1.598 billion.
The Spanish and Slovak projects will produce battery cells, while the Moroccan facility will manufacture cathode materials for lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries.
Volkswagen’s battery subsidiary PowerCo will retain a 51% stake in the Valencia venture, with Gotion holding 49%. Gotion will hold 51% in each of the Slovak and Moroccan ventures, while PowerCo will own the remaining stakes.
The Spanish project targets annual battery production capacity of 29.1 gigawatt-hours, while the Slovak facility is planned to produce 8.4 gigawatt-hours annually, according to Gotion’s filing.
The Moroccan project aims to manufacture 100,000 metric tons of LFP cathode materials a year, primarily supplying the two European battery ventures. Investment will be made in stages.
“This marks a major breakthrough for both companies,” said Volkswagen technology chief Thomas Schmall.
Volkswagen said the partnership would diversify supplies of key cathode materials and strengthen the competitiveness of Europe’s battery industry.
The projects are subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions, including approval by Gotion’s shareholders.

The industrial sector, however, continued to face challenges. Gross value added in industry declined by 1.8 percent in 2025.
On the expenditure side, household and government final consumption expenditure increased 0.9 percent in real terms. Gross fixed capital formation was another major driver of growth, rising 4.3 percent in real terms in 2025 after declining for two consecutive years. ■

Interview: Ghana needs deliberate strategies to leverage China's zero-tariff offer, says foreign trade leader

by Justice Lee Adoboe
ACCRA, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- A Ghanaian foreign trade leader has hailed China's zero-tariff treatment as a crucial opportunity for African countries.
Samson Asaki Awingobit, executive secretary of the Importers and Exporters Association of Ghana, told Xinhua that the zero-tariff offer is something Ghanaian exporters have desired for a long time.
"This offer is excellent news from China, giving us tariff-free market access," said Awingobit.
For the country to realize the full benefits, Awingobit said that Ghana needs to develop deliberate strategies to enhance export competitiveness so that Ghanaian traders, small-scale and large-scale manufacturers, and agricultural producers can access the Chinese market with meaningful export returns to the country.
"We would like to see more of our exports going into the Chinese market, and so now that they have given us zero tariffs, we need as a country to engage among ourselves and seek an understanding of the Chinese market to know which of our products are in high demand," he stressed.
With a firm knowledge of product lines in high demand in the Chinese market, Awingobit said Ghanaians could also develop what they can produce with a comparative advantage to satisfy those demands.
Moreover, he said that understanding the demands in the Chinese market and their consumer behavior would enable Ghana to adopt a regional approach to meeting these identified needs.
"We need to understand the specific needs of each province and identify the strengths and comparative advantages of different regions in Ghana so that we can build capacity and educate traders on how to leverage this new opportunity," he stressed.
According to Awingobit, Ghanaians appreciate the new trade relationship with China, and "that must translate into tangible benefits and transformations in the economy and in the lives of the people."
With the size of the Chinese market and the right strategies, he called for efforts to "do more volumes because the Chinese market is huge."
Even if a province is going to purchase from Ghana, Awingobit believed, that represents a significant demand, and it is time for Ghana to work hard toward meeting the demands.
In May, China expanded its zero-tariff treatment to cover all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic ties.
China is Ghana's largest trading partner, as bilateral trade grew by 19.3 percent year on year to 14.1 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, according to the Chinese Embassy to Ghana. ■

Mu Xinyue becomes first female Asian Games esports gold medalist (updated)
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-01
00:19:25 CST
01:19:25 KST

Mu Xinyue (C) of team China celebrates with her teammates after the 1v4 asymmetrical survival game [Identity V - Asian Games Version] final of Esports between team China and team Japan at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 in Tokoname of Aichi Prefecture, Japan, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Fei)
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- China's Mu Xinyue became the first female athlete to win an Asian Games esports gold medal after China defeated Japan in the Identity V Asian Games Version final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Wednesday.
Asian Games esports events are open to both male and female athletes, but men continue to make up the overwhelming majority of registered athletes. According to registration data for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, more than 500 athletes were registered for esports, with only 14 of them women.
"When I first started competing, I never imagined that I would be able to win a gold medal on the Asian Games stage," Mu said. "When the national anthem was played and the gold medal was around my neck, I was so excited and happy. I think this may be the happiest moment of my life."
Identity V is an asymmetrical competitive game in which each round consists of two halves, with the two teams taking turns playing as survivors and hunters. Four players compete on the survivor side while one plays as the hunter, with points awarded based on the number of survivors who escape and the hunter's eliminations.
China's Identity V squad consists of hunters Shi Xiangwei and Sun Le, and survivors Lu Shujia, Chen Mingming, Lu Yahui, Fan Siqi and Mu. Mu, whose in-game ID is "Tao Wan'an," is the only female member of China's esports delegation at the Games.
The final was tightly contested. The two sides tied the opening two rounds 4-4 and 5-5 before China took the third round 7-2 to gain the upper hand. The fourth round ended in another 4-4 tie, sending the match into a decisive fifth round. China took a 3-1 lead in the first half of the fifth round, which was enough to secure the victory.
Shi, whose in-game ID is "Nianjin," said competing at the Asian Games carried a different sense of responsibility from playing in a professional league.
"First of all, there is a change of identity, and there is also greater responsibility on your shoulders," Shi said. "You can be nervous and you can feel pressure, but you shouldn't let the pressure and nerves affect your performance in the game. Accept the nerves and the pressure, face them naturally, and just play your normal game."
The final was interrupted by a technical issue between the two halves of the fourth round, with play suspended for nearly 30 minutes before competition resumed. The interruption was caused by an on-site network cable issue.
Mu said she remained calm during the unexpected stoppage.
"I didn't really have any emotional fluctuations at that time," the 20-year-old said. "We just waited to see what the referees and the organizers would decide. All we needed to do was wait patiently."
Esports made its Asian Games debut as a demonstration sport at Jakarta 2018 before becoming an official medal sport at Hangzhou in 2023. The number of medal events has increased from seven in Hangzhou to 11 at Aichi-Nagoya, with Identity V Asian Games Version making its Asian Games debut.
China entered four of the 11 esports events at Aichi-Nagoya -- Naraka: Bladepoint, Honor of Kings, Game for Peace Asian Games Version and Identity V Asian Games Version. China won gold in Naraka: Bladepoint and Honor of Kings and silver in Game for Peace Asian Games Version before adding the Identity V gold on Wednesday, concluding its esports campaign with three gold medals and one silver. ■

Feature: China Harbor's dredging of Tema Port to boost Ghana's maritime trade
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-01
00:19:22 CST
01:19:22 KST

by Justice Lee Adoboe
ACCRA, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Ghana is advancing efforts to cement its position as the maritime trade hub in West and Central Africa with major dredging work by Chinese marine construction firm China Harbor Engineering Company Ltd. (CHEC) at the old section of the eastern port of Tema to create deeper berthing capacity to accommodate bigger and more vessels.
The dredging, which began in September 2025, will deepen the port to minus 14 meters, with a dredging area of 2.8 million cubic meters.
Liu Jing, country manager of CHEC, told Xinhua in a recent interview that the firm deployed its Tiankun dredging vessel to carry out the Tema Port dredging operation. The vessel is the most sophisticated self-propelled cutter suction dredger in Asia with a conveyance capacity among the world's most advanced.
Liu said the need for the Tiankun dredging vessel was due to the nature of the terrain of the Tema Port, which involved the presence of a giant volume of extremely hard rock, "specifically, strongly weathered and moderately weathered rocks that have reached a very high degree of hardness that required advanced dredging technology to crack and excavate."
He noted that Tema is home to some of Ghana's toughest rock formations, with certain layers exhibiting very high megapascal ratings. "We had to change our approach during construction, depending on the changes in different sections, and optimize our approach along the way," he said.
Without a world-class cutter suction dredger like the Tiankun vessel, excavation would have been tough, according to the official.
"The Tiankun dredging vessel has played an excellent role in the whole process, not only in excavation but also in conveying the excavated rock to the shore through its transport system, effectively achieving reclamation," Liu noted, adding that the company has also employed a large pool of local Ghanaian workers under the project.
Tema Port Harbor Master, Bramwell Tawiah, praised CHEC for the speed of the dredging. He gave an example that when Ghana had only one cement manufacturing facility, the volume of clinker imports was minimal; however, the situation has changed due to the emergence of new cement factories, which are now importing larger volumes of clinker.
"With more growth in the economy, we began to see more competitors and an increase in clinker imports, which prompted us to re-strategize by developing a new berth for bulk clinker imports," he added.
Maritime policy expert Albert Derrick Fiatui described the dredging works by CHEC as strategic and timely, given the increasing volumes the country's seaport has been attracting recently.
Fiatui, who is Executive Director for the policy think tank Center for International Maritime Affairs, Ghana, said that because the port of Tema is the core of marine activities in the subregion, many landlocked countries in West and Central Africa transport their cargo through it.
"We know that the dredging involves approximately 2.8 million cubic meters of material, which will allow giant vessels to enter the port, improve our turnaround time, and make access to larger vessels a reality-something that every port strives for. Once you get a bigger berth, you can take any kind of vessel into your country, and the economy will benefit," the expert averred.
He added that, with the increasing volumes of imports and competition in the West and Central African subregion, Ghana needed the dredging to consolidate its position as the maritime hub in West Africa and Central Africa as well as the Sahel. "Ghana's blue economy is taking shape now and everybody is pleased and embracing this project," he said.
On his part, Samson Asaki Awingobit, Executive Secretary of the Importers and Exporters Association of Ghana, told Xinhua that the dredging work being done by CHEC is a significant game-changer for maritime trade in Ghana, to improve livelihoods and create more quality jobs.
"More business will come in after they finish the dredging. When trade volumes are arriving, it's going to raise demand for labor and skilled personnel. Hence, the jobs created would be both direct and indirect. They (CHEC) are always on time," Awingobit highlighted. ■

MOGADISHU, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Maritime forces from Somalia's Puntland State have rescued the Palau-flagged oil tanker MT Honor (Honor 25) off the coast of Bandarbeyla in northeastern Somalia.
In a statement released Tuesday evening, the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF) confirmed that the vessel and its 17 crew members were safe.
Held since April 21, the ship was freed in an operation that resulted in the arrest of 16 Somali pirates, while five crew members were killed by the hijackers before the rescue operation.

The vessel, which was hijacked while carrying 18,500 barrels of fuel bound for Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia, was freed during a targeted operation after an intelligence-led intervention disrupted the hijackers' defense plans.
This marked the second successful anti-piracy rescue operation conducted by Puntland maritime forces within a month.
Somalia's extensive coastline remains vulnerable to piracy despite years of international naval patrols and counter-piracy operations. ■

Romania’s political crisis intensifies as Parliament rejects pro-EU PM
Siegfried Muresan’s loss of the confidence motion increases the prospect for snap elections.
Romania’s pro-European Prime Minister-designate Siegfried Muresan has failed to win a parliamentary vote of confidence, prolonging a political crisis seen as a boost for the rising far right.
Muresan, a liberal European Parliament member who was the latest of three designated prime ministers, secured only 182 votes out of the 233 required to secure the confidence motion on Wednesday, according to the official count.

list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Why the world should care about the far right’s rise in Germany
- list 2 of 3Europe’s centrists are finally paying the price of their extremism
- list 3 of 3Switzerland’s neutrality vote is asking the wrong question
The far-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR) largely boycotted the vote.
The 45-year-old had proposed what he described as a “reform-oriented” governing programme under his centre-right National Liberal Party (PNL), which teamed up with the Save Romania Union party, or USR, and the small ethnic Hungarian UDMR party.
President Nicusor Dan said he would nominate a new prime minister candidate on Monday afternoon, after holding talks with the leaders of the parliamentary parties, to avoid snap elections.
Romania saw the collapse of a pro-European coalition government in May, when governing social democrats, together with the opposition far right, ousted liberal Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan in a no-confidence motion at that time.
The far right, which comprises about a third of Parliament, threatened to impeach the president if he does not call early elections once the conditions are met.
Romania, a member of the EU and NATO that borders Ukraine, has not held snap elections since the fall of communism in 1989.
Political analyst Cristian Pirvulescu told the AFP news agency that snap elections would lead to another fragmented Parliament, but with an emboldened far right.
“Early elections mean that, from the moment they are called, it would take four months before a new government could be formed,” Pirvulescu told AFP. “Due to political instability, Romania finds itself in a very complicated economic situation. Four months is already a very long time.”
The country of 19 million has been struggling for months with the highest public deficit and inflation in the European Union.

Journalists from Egypt fact checking site ‘forcibly disappeared’
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
16:17:04 UTC
01:17:04 KST

Breadcrumb
Investigative journalists from Egyptian fact-checking platform Matsada2sh ‘forcibly disappeared’
Independent Egyptian fact-checking platform Matsada2sh announced on Tuesday that its entire editorial team have been forcibly disappeared by security forces, with no reasons given.
The platform, which is titled after the Arabic word for ‘don’t believe it’ said the raid and detention took place on 28 September, identifying two of the journalists who were forcibly disappeared as Mohammed Ashraf and Abdullah Qadri.
The platform said in a statement that they were detained after a raid on their homes, with their phones and laptops being confiscated, as well as damage to some of their possessions.
It later said a further four journalists had been arrested.
They added that there has been no clear reason issued as to why they were detained or why they could be under investigation.
“While we affirm our full responsibility for the content published by Matsada2sh, we also affirm that the platform is a well-known journalistic entity that has been openly practicing its work for years, and has gained significant credibility,” the statement reads.
“Mohammed Ashraf and Abdullah Qadri are well-known journalists who practice their journalistic work openly…we hold the relevant authorities fully responsible for the safety and fate of our two colleagues, and we demand the immediate disclosure of the reasons behind their arrest and details on the entity holding them,” it continued.
"In a further escalation of security measures targeting journalists at Matsadaash, journalists Mohamed Mahmoud and Omar Hilal have been arrested, bringing the total number of Matsadaash journalists detained in recent hours to six," the platform said later on its Facebook page.
The Matsa2dash platform said it demands the journalists be granted their full legal rights and be allowed to communicate with their lawyers and families.
Abdalla Nasef, political analyst and host of Tahrir Podcast, told The New Arab that the move signals an even tighter iron fist policy by Egyptian authorities where not just journalism is targeted, but fact-checking platforms too.
"More revealing is that it wasn’t a journalist or two but the entire newsroom. “Matsad2sh” (the name of the platform: “Don’t Believe”) doesn’t publish op-eds; they fact-check government officials’ statements and even other journalists—regardless of political affiliation—while occasionally investigating and exposing corruption," he said.
"Overall, the message now is that if you aren’t controlled by the state, whether directly or indirectly, you will be went after," Nasef explained.
According to Nasef, those disappeared will likely appear before state security in the coming days and later potentially be released.
Sara Qudah, Middle East and North Africa Regional Director for the Committee to Protect Journalists, told The New Arab that action must be taken to find the whereabouts of the journalists and secure their release.
"CPJ is appalled by the arrests of Egyptian journalists Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emeira, Abdallah Qadry, Islam Barakat, Omar Helal, Mohamed Mahmoud, and Mohamed Adel, effectively detaining Matsadaash investigative media platform's entire newsroom," she said.
"Egyptian authorities must disclose their whereabouts, ensure their safety and legal rights, and release them immediately. The arrests mark an alarming escalation in Egypt’s crackdown on independent journalism," she added.
Hossam Bahgat, the director of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), is providing legal representation to the journalists on the Matsa2dash team.
A follow-up report from EIPR on Wednesday said that six members of the team had been detained, with the other journalists, including Omar Helal, Mohammed Mahmoud, Mohammed Adel and Islam Barakat, being arrested on Tuesday.
The organisation called on Attorney General Mohammed Shawky to open an urgent investigation to determine the whereabouts and condition of the six journalists, as well as the circumstances surrounding their arrest by plain-clothed officers.
The group noted that this is not the first time members of Matsa2dash have been targeted with arrests, adding that in August 2023, one of the platform’s editors was detained for 48 hours by a security agency before they were released.
The Matsa2dash platform is well known around the region for its debunking of fake news from Egypt and other countries in the Middle East. It started working in 2018 and has a team of independent researchers and reporters.
International rights groups have criticised Egypt for its crackdown on press freedoms and silencing of any form of dissent.
Earlier this year, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said authorities had “systematically dismantled basic freedoms and suffocated civic space”.
Amr Magdi, senior Middle East and Africa researcher at HRW said: The authorities are crushing peaceful dissent with impunity and at the same time failing in their basic duty to manage the economy in a way that fulfils people’s rights.”

Proekt investigation finds that Putin’s reported partner Alina Kabaeva accompanied him to Kazakhstan in 2017
Vladimir Putin and Alina Kabaeva were both in Kazakhstan in February 2017, when Putin met with the country’s then-president, Nursultan Nazarbayev, Proekt reported. The outlet’s journalists examined leaked data from Russia’s Federal Border Service.
Kabaeva, who has been described as Putin’s longtime partner and the mother of his sons, reportedly flew to Almaty on February 23 aboard a private Embraer Legacy 650 jet and returned to Russia four days later, on February 27. Putin’s official visit to Kazakhstan began that same day, but he had arrived several days before the visit’s announced start. State media reports corroborated his early arrival, describing an informal meeting between Putin and Nazarbayev at the Shymbulak ski resort.
Proekt calls the trip the only documented instance of Kabaeva being abroad during one of Putin’s official visits, with her “effectively serving as first lady.” Her presence on the trip was not officially reported.
The aircraft Kabaeva flew on, registration number D-AHOI, was operated by Air Hamburg, which later became part of VistaJet. Proekt estimates the flight would have cost about $26,000. The same jet was also used over the years by the families of Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov, Investigative Committee head Alexander Bastrykin and Russian Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Patrushev.
Proekt suggests that Kabaeva may have accompanied Putin on other trips as well, citing his visit to Uzbekistan for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in June 2016. Putin arrived there on June 23, and Kabaeva returned to Moscow on June 30 on a scheduled Aeroflot flight. The leaked data contain no record of her departure from Russia. The record may be missing because of an error or because Kabaeva flew from Russia to Uzbekistan on a government aircraft.

The U.S. lifted its long-standing blanket ban on arms exports to Syria on Wednesday, allowing proposed defense sales and security services to Damascus to be considered on a case-by-case basis.
"The Department of State is amending the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) to remove Syria from the list of countries subject to a policy of denial for licenses and other approvals," the agency said in a public notice published in the Federal Register. The administrative rule formally takes effect Thursday.
The regulatory adjustment implements a decision authorized Aug. 19 by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who approved a revised defense trade framework permitting authorities to evaluate individual applications for military equipment and security service transactions bound for or originating in Syria.
The regulatory shift arrives as the Trump administration moves to normalize diplomatic and trade relations with Syria following the collapse of Bashar Assad's regime in late 2024.
Washington previously terminated comprehensive economic sanctions and removed Damascus from its State Sponsors of Terrorism list as part of a conditional engagement strategy with the new leadership headed by President Ahmed al-Sharaa.
The Federal Register document is unpublished as of reporting at 1600GMT and is expected to be released Thursday.

U.S. Air Force Awards $64 Million Contract for High-Altitude Balloon Prototype
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
16:14:41 UTC
01:14:41 KST

The U.S. Air Force has awarded Aerostar Technical Solutions a $64.4 million contract under the Swamp Gas project to develop a prototype high-altitude balloon.
The U.S. Department of War published the contract announcement on September 28. The agreement with Aerostar was awarded without competition.
Under the project, the company is to develop a minimum viable prototype (MVP) to address an urgent operational need for a high-altitude balloon.
The work will be performed in Arlington, Virginia, and is scheduled for completion by March 23, 2028. At the time the contract was awarded, $57.7 million had been obligated from fiscal year 2025 research, development, test, and evaluation funds, along with another $6.27 million from fiscal year 2026 funds.
The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base manages the contract. The intended mission of the future balloon, its payload, and the unit that will operate it have not been disclosed.
The Defense Blog reported that Aerostar has long worked with the U.S. military on using stratospheric platforms for communications, reconnaissance, and surveillance.
In particular, the company is developing the Thunderhead family of high-altitude balloons, which can remain in the stratosphere for extended periods and maneuver by changing altitude and using air currents. In March 2025, one of these systems completed a record-breaking 336-day flight. Aerostar markets such systems as platforms for persistent surveillance and reconnaissance and for providing resilient communications.
Militarnyi previously reported that in August 2026, the U.S. Army tested stratospheric balloons in Poland during the Cold Raptor exercise. The platforms operate at altitudes of about 18-21 kilometers and can carry reconnaissance sensors, communications equipment and electronic warfare systems. During the exercise, service members practiced launching, controlling, monitoring and recovering the balloons.
High-altitude balloons are also being used in the Russo-Ukrainian war.
In September 2025, Russian sources reported the mass use of unidentified balloons simultaneously with a Ukrainian long-range drone raid. They were detected over the Moscow region, Chuvashia, Tatarstan, the Yaroslavl region, and the Tver region. According to Russian reports, some of the objects were flying at an altitude of about 10 kilometers.
In Ukraine, balloons have also been tested as airborne communications relays. In 2025, Himera Radios and Aerobavovna tested the B1 relay for HIMERA tactical radios, raising it to altitudes of 500 and 800 meters.
Testing confirmed stable communications at a distance of 32 kilometers, while mounting the relay on a balloon significantly expanded the radio horizon.

Stellantis CEO reconfirms 2026 guidance, says turnaround plan continues as automaker's shares hit new low

Unknown Publisher

01:14:12 KST

DETROIT — Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa on Wednesday reconfirmed the company's 2026 guidance and longer-term cash flow targets as U.S. shares of the embattled automaker trade at an all-time low.
"We are completely committed and we are convinced that we will do that," Filosa said Wednesday about Stellantis' forecast for this year of a mid-single-digit percentage increase in net revenue and a low-single-digit adjusted operating margin.
Filosa also reconfirmed the company is aiming to be cash flow positive by next year and generate more than 3 billion euros ($3.4 billion) of free cash flow in 2028.
The stock ended Tuesday at a new closing low for the company's U.S. shares, contributing to a roughly 60% loss so far this year. The stock is on track for its worst annual performance since the automaker was formed through the merger of Fiat Chrysler and PSA Groupe in January 2021.
Shares of the company fell further Wednesday, closing the day 1.58% lower, at $4.36 a share.
The trans-Atlantic automaker has been executing a roughly $70 billion turnaround plan following margin dilution and yearslong sales declines, especially in North America and the U.S.
Filosa's turnaround strategy has included focusing on regional brands to boost sales, such as Ram and Jeep in the U.S., but it is not cutting down its vast portfolio of 14 automotive brands. The plan's core pillars are "sharper management" of the brand portfolio, new investments, enhanced partnerships, an optimized manufacturing footprint, "excellence in execution," and empowerment of the company's regions and local teams.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Tom Narayan on Tuesday in an investor note said despite public comments to keep the company together, the firm views a "break-up as a plausible longer-term scenario" for Stellantis.
The goal is for the company to achieve positive free cash flow by 2027. Free cash flow for the automaker was a loss of 4.5 billion euros last year.
"The mantra of the reset is around freedom of choice," Filosa, who became CEO in June 2025, said Wednesday during an Automotive News event in Detroit. "It's around listening more to the customer."

MI5 accuses Chinese research institute of funding research to support espionage
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
16:12:49 UTC
01:12:49 KST

Mucahithan Avcioglu
30 September 2026•Update: 30 September 2026
MI5 accused a Chinese research institute of funding academic work to strengthen Beijing’s espionage capabilities, urging UK universities to review their collaborations with the organization.
Britain’s domestic security service said in a public espionage alert that the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI) has strong ties to China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS), the country’s civilian intelligence and security service. The institute is also sometimes referred to as the China Academy of General Technology.
“MI5 has identified that the primary purpose of CGTRI is to fund academic research that directly improves MSS technical capability for espionage,” it said.
More than 100 UK-linked academics have contributed to research projects funded by the MSS through CGTRI, according to MI5.
The projects covered artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, covert communications systems and steganography, a technique for concealing information within other material.
MI5 said the activity supported Chinese espionage and threatened UK national security. It acknowledged that some academics might not have known the institute was funding the Chinese research projects to which they contributed.
The agency urged UK academic institutions to review ongoing or planned collaborations with CGTRI immediately and advised researchers working with Chinese institutions to establish the ultimate source of funding.
It said many institutions and individuals would have engaged with CGTRI in good faith because its connections to Chinese intelligence had been concealed.
MI5 warned institutions and researchers to consider potential criminal consequences under the National Security Act 2023, particularly provisions concerning assistance to a foreign intelligence service and receipt of material benefits from one.
Institutions or individuals continuing research ultimately funded by CGTRI should seek independent legal advice, it said.

US removes Syria from arms export ban list under revised defense trade policy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
16:11:01 UTC
01:11:01 KST

Yasin Gungor
30 September 2026•Update: 30 September 2026
The US said Wednesday that it lifted its long-standing blanket ban on arms exports to Syria, clearing the way for case-by-case reviews of defense sales and security services to Damascus.
"The Department of State is amending the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) to remove Syria from the list of countries subject to a policy of denial for licenses and other approvals," the agency said in a public notice published in the Federal Register. The administrative rule formally takes effect Thursday.
The regulatory adjustment implements a decision authorized Aug. 19 by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who approved a revised defense trade framework permitting authorities to evaluate individual applications for military equipment and security service transactions bound for or originating in Syria.
The regulatory shift arrives as the Trump administration moves to normalize diplomatic and trade relations with Syria following the collapse of Bashar al-Assad's government in late 2024.
Washington previously terminated comprehensive economic sanctions and removed Damascus from its State Sponsors of Terrorism list as part of a conditional engagement strategy with the new leadership headed by President Ahmed al-Sharaa.
The Federal Register document is unpublished as of reporting at 1600GMT and is expected to be released Thursday.

Antisemitic incidents in Spain rose 14.5% in 2025, Spanish Jewish group tells Senate in report
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
16:09:54 UTC
01:09:54 KST

The Federation of Jewish Communities of Spain (FCJE) presented its annual report on antisemitism for the year 2025 to the Spanish Senate on Monday, documenting a general increase in reported incidents compared to the previous year, detailing episodes of hostility across public, institutional, educational, and sports spheres. The report was conducted by the Spanish Observatory on Antisemitism, an initiative of the FCJE and the Movement against Intolerance (MCI).
According to the report, in 2025, 221 antisemitic incidents were recorded, representing a 14.51% increase compared to the 193 cases registered in 2024. The report noted that the months with the highest hostile activity coincided with the anniversary of October 7, along with peaks in September and July. Furthermore, the report highlighted significant underreporting driven by fear of retaliation, distrust, or the emotional toll on victims.
The report emphasized that Israel has been at the center of hostilities that have spilled over into Jewish communities, institutions, and sympathetic citizens.
Among the unprecedented institutional and cultural events mentioned in the report is the decision by Spain’s state-owned public broadcaster, RTVE [Radio Televisión Española], not to participate in the Eurovision Song Contest in response to Israel’s inclusion, alongside active institutional pressure campaigns urging other European public broadcasters to force Israel’s exclusion or promote a collective withdrawal.
The report also compiled cases of graffiti, property damage, protests, and expressions of hate speech on social media. Concluding its findings, the report stated that “the totality of the incidents described in this report evidences a worrisome normalization of antisemitic discourses and behaviors that require a firm, coordinated response sustained over time.”
Findings on antisemitism brought to Senate
The findings of the report were formally unveiled during an event at the Spanish Senate, which brought together political figures and community leaders to discuss both the past year’s data and the evolving landscape into 2026.
Held with various senators and acting Ambassador Dana Erlich in attendance, the gathering featured opening remarks from center-right Senate President Pedro Rollán, who committed to continuing the fight against antisemitism as one of the great evils afflicting society.
FCJE president notes dangerous antisemitism resurgence in Spain post-Oct. 7
Taking the floor during the presentation, FCJE President David Obadía detailed a dangerous resurgence of antisemitism in Spain since October 7, 2023, and how Spanish Jews experience it day-by-day, while also calling on authorities for their support to denounce and legally prosecute antisemites.
Speakers noted that this upward trajectory has continued into 2026, pointing to ongoing examples such as boycotts targeting individuals and institutions connected to Israel, hostile chants directed at Jews in television broadcasts and sports venues, and political statements such as recent remarks by far-left Youth Minister Sira Abed Rego, expressing a desire for a “free Palestine from the river to the sea.”
FCJE and the Spanish Observatory on Antisemitism told The Jerusalem Post of three recent incidents that, in their view, highlighted the seriousness of the current situation.
One was the remarks made by Rego, the youth minister.
Another was that the “organizers of Granada’s CULTUR-ALH International Festival of Art, Literature and Humanities withdrew Argentine writer Ariana Harwicz’s invitation just days before the festival began, following objections to her participation from pro-Palestinian groups over her public positions on Israel and her opposition to cultural boycotts of Israel.”
Yet another, they noted, was that “German insurer Allianz withdrew its sponsorship of Madrid’s Festival of Ideas following threats by a number of participants to boycott the festival over the company’s financial ties to Israel.”
The FCJE told the Senate: “Taken together, these recent incidents illustrate the complex and wide-ranging nature of antisemitism in Spain. The FCJE calls on public authorities to take appropriate action and on Spanish society as a whole to combat antisemitism, which undermines the foundations of a democratic and pluralistic society.”

Israeli ministers call for increased military action after flydubai incident

Ministers in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government called for increased military action on all regional fronts following what Israeli officials described as an attempted hijacking of a flydubai flight carrying more than 100 Israeli passengers on Wednesday.
Ministers and opposition politicians praised the Israeli passengers aboard the flybubai aircraft, saying that they saved many lives and potentially prevented a disaster on the scale of 9/11. Netanyahu confirmed that one of the pilots on the flight had carried out a stabbing attack.
Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich was the first member of the government to issue a statement after the incident, calling for action to be taken against “whoever tried to crash a plane and murder 180 Israelis. He and every state or terrorist organization that sent him,” he wrote.
He called for Israel to “address the intent and not the results.”
There is currently no evidence to suggest the suspected hijacker had backing from a foreign actor.
National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir shared a report from Channel 14 saying that the hijacker had planned an attack akin to 9/11. This report has not been verified, and the motive of the pilot has not been clarified at this time.
Calling for increased military action on all fronts, he said that “Israel has done tremendous work over the past two and a half years, but it must not stop and must continue until achieving a complete victory in Iran, Lebanon, Gaza, and Judea and Samaria.”
“The naive perception that our enemies value life and should be shown mercy received another reminder this morning in the form of a terrorist who planned to crash a plane and murder the 180 Israelis on board.”
“Terror is an evil that must never be met with any agreement other than defeating it and wiping it off the face of the earth,” Ben-Gvir added.
Culture and Sport Minister Miki Zohar stated, “Thank God Almighty for the great miracles and for the Israeli heroes who showed tremendous resourcefulness and saved many lives. Israel’s enemies will pay dearly.”
Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar’s office said it had no comment on the incident when approached by The Jerusalem Post for the minister’s response.
Asked what immediate steps Sa’ar had taken after the incident of the flybubai plane was first reported to ensure the safe return of the Israelis on the plane, his office told the Post it would not provide details at this time and that the Prime Minister’s Office was managing the incident.
Transportation Minister Miri Regev had requested that the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) halt all flights by the airline flydubai entering and exiting the country following the incident, a source in the ministry confirmed to the Post.
According to the source, Regev’s request came after unverified reports indicating that the co-pilot suspected of hijacking the plane may have been of Omani origin. Flydubai’s agreement to operate in Israel explicitly states that all pilots must be from countries that have normalized relations with Israel, which does not include Oman.
Netanyahu and Regev later arrived at Ben-Gurion Airport to greet the passengers who landed back in Israel on Wednesday evening.
Party leaders in the opposition bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu in the October 27 election praised the passengers who were on the plane, while also condemning the government for attempting to use the incident for political gain.
Their comments came in response to reports and attempts by Netanyahu’s political allies and supporters to portray the incident as vindication of the prime minister’s warnings a day earlier about possible attacks on Israel ahead of the Knesset election.
Lapid: Flydubai incident was not mentioned during security briefing on Tuesday
Earlier in the day, opposition leader Yair Lapid clarified that the flydubai incident had not been mentioned, even indirectly, during the security briefing he received from Netanyahu on Tuesday night.
Leader of The Democrats party Yair Golan said that he was “filled with pride in the brave Israelis who, in a moment of danger, displayed extraordinary resourcefulness and courage, though adding that he “despised the disgraceful attempts by the ‘Hamas is an asset’ government to play cheap politics at the expense of that heroism.”
Yisrael Beytenu party leader MK Avigdor Liberman also praised the Israelis on the flight, while adding that “the attempt by the mouthpieces and government-affiliated figures to turn an incident involving the hijacking of a plane, when civilians were in danger and facing uncertainty, into political capital is disgraceful.”
Liberman added that nothing surprises him anymore about Netanyahu’s government.
“While people were fighting for their lives, they were looking for a way to manufacture a spin,” he added, vowing to soon replace “this insane government.”
Former prime minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the B’Yachad party, also praised the Israelis on the plane, saying, “Where else in the world would you find a people like this, where civilians calmly take control of an armed assailant at an altitude of thousands of meters while the plane is in a dive, saving the lives of 180 people?”
“The entire people of Israel are proud of you and salute you for your bravery and resourcefulness,” he said.

A major amusement park in California confirmed that it will permanently shut down its famous X2 roller coaster following mounting reports of severe brain injuries and multiple lawsuits.
“While X2 consistently passed a multitude of safety tests, we have decided to close the ride because we believe it’s the right thing to do,” Six Flags Magic Mountain Park President Brian Oerding said in an operational update Tuesday.

U.K. leader says Iran believed to have "played a part" in air base incident
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
16:07:30 UTC
01:07:30 KST

U.K. believes Iran "played a part" in incident near RAF Fairford base used by U.S. forces, prime minister says
London — The British government believes Iran "played a part" in the incident over the weekend at the RAF Fairford air base in England, which has been used by U.S. warplanes carrying out strikes on Iran, U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Wednesday.
Burnham's remarks to the BBC were the first confirmation by the British government of its assessment of the incident, which saw five men — all British nationals in their mid-20s — arrested near RAF Fairford early Sunday morning on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act. They were all released on bail the following day, however, even though the police had the right to hold them for up to 14 days under U.K. counterterrorism laws.
Their quick release drew criticism from President Trump and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. But it also prompted questions in the U.K. as to whether the authorities had overreacted.
U.K. counterterrorism police said no explosives were found in extensive searches of the three vehicles operated by the men, only some fuel and a number of large, mostly empty plastic drums.
There were reports by local media, unconfirmed by authorities, that the men could have been fuel thieves trying to steal diesel from farms in the rural area or possibly even from the air base itself. But Burnham indicated Wednesday that a more serious plot could have been in play.
"There are strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened over the weekend at RAF Fairford, but of course it remains an ongoing, complex and serious police investigation, and of course we are working closely with our colleagues in the United States of America," the prime minister told the BBC.
"We will say more in due course, but we can confirm our belief that we believe Iran to have played a part," he said.
Asked why the suspects were released so quickly on bail, he said, "people need to understand that when it says released — that isn't as people might think. It's obviously with the strictest possible bail conditions."
Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, who heads the London Metropolitan Police force's Counter Terror Policing unit, said Monday that the men remained under investigation and would be monitored closely.
"The authorities have this under the strongest grip and closest control, and I can assure you of that," Burnham told the BBC, stressing that U.K. authorities had been "talking to our counterparts in the United States all week to explain what is happening here, how things are being done."
He said he had "complete confidence in the way British security services are handling this."
Working for Iran "knowingly or unknowingly"?
Iranian authorities have warned that any bases used to attack the country would be considered legitimate targets, but the Iranian Embassy in London said in a statement shared Monday on social media that the regime "categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations published by some British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Iran" to the incident.
Taylor, the head of the London police's counterterror unit, told reporters Monday the incident "may be activity committed by proxies, or individuals either knowingly or unknowingly, working on behalf of a foreign state."
Iran has, like Russia, been accused of using individuals who may be unaware they are even working for a foreign state to conduct sabotage attacks across Western Europe.
The Iran-aligned group Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia — or The Islamic Movement of the Companions of the Righteous (IMCR) — has claimed responsibility for several incidents over the past few months, including attacks on synagogues in the Netherlands and Belgium, and multiple attacks on north London's Jewish community.
A representative of the group told CBS News in March that it would "keep threatening U.S. and Israeli interests worldwide until we've avenged every child in Gaza, Iran, Lebanon, and the resistance nations," and it urged people "to stay away from Zionist and American interests."
In July, the U.K. government said the elite Quds Force of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps "almost certainly directed IMCR attacks across Europe."
Experts have characterized those incidents as part of a growing pattern of Iran and Russia outsourcing sabotage by recruiting sometimes unsuspecting people, often young men, to carry out low-level attacks for financial compensation.
On Tuesday, law enforcement authorities in NATO member Estonia said they had determined an arson attack against a defense industry company in mid-August was a "deliberate and pre-planned act commissioned by Russian security services."

EU supports modernization of Ukrainian Armed Forces training centers
Ukrinform reports this, citing the Ministry of Defense.
The project envisages improving living conditions, developing comfortable infrastructure and upgrading existing facilities.
The project will be implemented under the auspices of the European External Action Service (EEAS), the Military Planning and Conduct Capability (MPCC), and the EU Military Assistance Mission in support of Ukraine (EUMAM Ukraine).
The charitable foundation Come Back Alive will be responsible for implementing the project in close cooperation with the Ministry of Defense.
The main focus will be on developing the infrastructure of Ukrainian Armed Forces training centers.
The goal is to create a modern training environment and the conditions necessary for high-quality military training.
“Modernized centers enable us to train military personnel based on real-world combat experience. We thank the European Union for its support and every partner country that has already joined or will join the project,” Deputy Defense Minister Liubov Halan said.
Training in Ukraine is as fundamental to defense as ammunition and equipment, because weapons are ineffective without trained personnel, she noted.
The project is being implemented at the initiative of the EU. All partner countries may contribute to its funding, while Denmark serves as the fund administrator.
The Ukrainian and Danish defense ministries previously signed a Letter of Intent on implementing a project to modernize one of the Ukrainian Armed Forces’ training centers. Under the agreement, Denmark allocated about €33 million for training infrastructure, living and sanitary facilities, equipment and drones for training Ukrainian defenders.
As previously reported by Ukrinform,EU member states agreed to extend the EUMAM Ukraine mission to train Ukrainian military personnel for another two years.

Brexit referendum 'possible' in Labour election manifesto, says Burnham

Andy Burnham has said it is "possible" a future Labour election manifesto could promise a new in-out referendum on the European Union.
The prime minister told the BBC a referendum "wouldn't be the right thing to do right now" but the UK needed to "consider the options" for its relationship with the EU as "where we are isn't good enough".
It comes after he pledged in his Labour conference speech on Tuesday to explore closer ties with the bloc at a summit later this year.
The move could set up a huge dividing line at the next general election, with the Conservatives accusing Burnham of trying to "reopen old wounds by restarting the battles of the Brexit years".
As a candidate in the Makerfield by-election that propelled his return to Parliament, Burnham had promised not to "re-run" Brexit arguments and said he was "not proposing that the UK considers rejoining the EU".
In an interview with BBC political editor Chris Mason, Burnham was challenged over whether he was reopening divisive arguments about rejoining the EU, despite promising not to in May.
In response, the PM said: "No, I'm not proposing that, am I? I am saying that in a context when we're looking at a 10-year plan for Britain, Britain needs to consider the options as to where we will be.
"That is way before you even get to anything that's put before the public, this is about now just looking at what are the broad options for our relationship."
He suggested these options could include staying "exactly as we are", a closer relationship similar to that being discussed by the EU and Canada or rejoining the EU customs union.
However, Burnham stressed that "to leap back to a proposal and a referendum on it wouldn't be the right thing to do right now".
Pressed over whether including an in-out referendum in a future Labour manifesto was a possibility, Burnham said: "Yes, things are possible. I think where we are isn't good enough."

Russia Draws Up Measures to Control Bear Population After Spate of Deadly Attacks
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
16:06:19 UTC
01:06:19 KST

The Russian government said on Wednesday it was drawing up urgent measures to control the population of brown bears that has spiraled out of control in some regions, with at least 22 people killed in attacks.
In the latest attack, reported by state media, a 23-year-old man out gathering berries was killed by a bear this week in Kamchatka, in Russia's far east.
Last week, a Russian woman in Siberia was fatally mauled by a bear in her garden, amid a nationwide spate of killings that experts blame on climate change and human incompetence.
"It is clear that as the population grows, so too does the number of problems. Systemic measures are needed to ensure that humans and animals can coexist safely and to maintain the necessary balance," said Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Patrushev.
"In this regard, the Russian government is currently preparing a series of priority measures," he said.
The government said it would look at lifting hunting quotas on brown bears, would establish regional population limits, give local authorities extra powers to control their numbers, and identify regions that need more financing to tackle the problem.
The population of brown bears has more than doubled in the last three decades to 308,000, in part due to shorter and milder winters. At least 22 people have been killed by bears across Russia, the world's largest country, since this spring, the RIA state news agency said.
Experts cited in Russian media have said bears have been forced to look further afield for food this year because an early and dry spring meant there was a lack of berries for them to feed on in September.
People are also guilty of leaving food waste out in the open where it attracts bears and of ignoring safety rules, experts say.
Investigators in Krasnoyarsk in Siberia — home to nearly 27,000 bears, according to environment ministry data — said last week that they had opened a criminal case into the local environment ministry, accusing it of negligence that led to the deaths of seven people in September alone.
The federal environment ministry has sought to play down the spate of attacks, saying that around 20 to 30 cases of bear attacks have been recorded annually in recent years, but that social media and smartphones are making such attacks seem more widespread.

The region is well connected to the Sea of Azov by both rivers and man-made canals and is known for its rich mineral deposits. It used to be the backbone of Ukraine’s coal and steel production.
Ukraine Calls Urgent OSCE Meeting Over Oleshky Crisis
While the Kremlin has long demanded full control of the regions as preconditions for any possible settlement, Ukraine continues to reject giving up its territory and sovereignty as a prerequisite for peace, although it frequently calls on Russia to agree to an unconditional ceasefire.
Putin has repeatedly questioned Ukraine’s legitimacy as an independent state, rejecting the sovereignty it gained after the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
During the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) held in New York last week, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov – representing Putin – said that the Kremlin will not pause its “special military operation” even during negotiations, adding that Ukraine would have kept its 1991 borders if the European nations had not “engaged in their shenanigans.”
The Kremlin has long described Ukraine as part of a broader “historical Russia,” while also accusing Kyiv, without evidence, of violating the rights of Russian speakers in Ukraine.
The Donbas, home to a large Russian-speaking population, is central to that narrative. It was also where Russia’s campaign to destabilize Ukraine began in 2014.
After illegally annexing Crimea, Moscow armed and backed separatists in the Donbas, who seized parts of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions, including both regional capitals.
Zelensky visits Lyman front
The latest announcement follows a visit by President Volodymyr Zelensky to the troops in the Lyman sector earlier on Wednesday, where he met corps, brigade and battalion commanders at the command post of the 66th Separate Mechanized Brigade.
The brigade has participated in the liberation of Novoselivka, Oleksandrivka, Yarova, Serednie, Shandryholove, and the area around Koroviy Yar, according to the Presidential Office.
During his visit, Zelensky was accompanied by Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara, Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) Mykhailo Drapaty, and Commander of the Air Assault Forces Oleh Apostol.
The discussions centered on defense procurement at the brigade level, with particular attention to pickup trucks, as well as strengthening the Unmanned Systems Forces (USF) and increasing funding for drones.
It also covered expanding and training military personnel, as well as streamlining procurement procedures.
The meeting came as Putin signed a fourth such decree on Monday, Sept. 28, increasing the size of Russia’s armed forces to 2.4 million, including 1.5 million active-duty military personnel.
The new ceiling is 15,500 higher than the one set out in a decree that took effect on Aug. 1, which put the military at 2,426,130 personnel, including 1,535,000 troops.
Operation ‘Vivaldi’
On Sunday, Sept. 27, Zelensky announced that the Ukrainian Defense Forces have achieved important battlefield results in the Lyman axis under Operation “Vivaldi.”
Citing a report from Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapatyi, he said Ukrainian units killed or wounded 10,660 Russian soldiers this week.
The operation was announced on Sept. 15 by the 3rd Army Corps, commanded by Brigadier General Andriy Biletsky, following weeks of strict informational silence.
In its first phase, the Ukrainian military cleared Russian infiltration pockets around Novoselivka, Yarova, Koroviahyi Yar and Oleksandrivka and liberated the village of Serednie, which Biletsky described as a “shaping, preparatory phase.”
On Sept. 20, Ukrainian Defense Forces announced the results of the second phase by saying that they had liberated Shandryholove and Derylove and established full control over Drobysheve.
Across both phases, the corps said it had recovered 125 square kilometers (48 square miles) of territory including 50 square kilometers (19 square miles) formally de-occupied.
Russian forces are believed to have lost around 800 soldiers in the second phase and more than 3,000 across both phases combined.

Appeals court halts execution of Tennessee woman less than two hours before lethal injection

US Supreme Court clears way for Tennessee execution of woman for murder
The US Supreme Court on Wednesday cleared the way for Tennessee to execute Christa Pike, 50, the state's first woman put to death in 200 years. The ruling came hours after a federal appeals court temporarily halted the lethal injection to consider claims that Pike's childhood sexual abuse was not adequately weighed at sentencing.
The US Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that Tennessee could proceed with its first execution of a woman in 200 years, clearing the way for Christa Pike to be put to death by lethal injection for murdering a schoolmate as an 18-year-old three decades ago.
The Tennessee Department of Correction said in a statement to Reuters afterwards that it planned "to move forward with the execution today."
Pike, 50, whose clemency petition highlighting childhood trauma and sexual abuse was denied by Governor Bill Lee on Monday, would also be the only person in the modern era of US capital punishment to be executed in Tennessee for a crime committed as a teenager.
In an order decided by its 6-3 conservative majority, the Supreme Court lifted a stay of execution that was granted by a three-judge panel of the 6th US Circuit Court of Appeals one hour before Pike had been scheduled to be put to death.
The appellate panel voted 2-1 to order a "short stay" to allow time to weigh Pike's claim that evidence of her childhood sexual abuse was not adequately considered during her sentencing.
But the Tennessee attorney general's office immediately asked the US Supreme Court to vacate the stay. And the high court's decision siding with Tennessee marked the final word on whether the execution was permitted to go forward before her death warrant expires at midnight CDT (0500 GMT).
The state did not give a precise new time frame for the execution, which was set to take place at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital.
If the state were to run out of time to conduct the execution, it would need to obtain a new warrant from the Tennessee Supreme Court, according to Robin Maher, executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center.
Read moreUS judge bars prosecutors from seeking death penalty against Luigi Mangione
Pike, now 50, and her boyfriend were convicted of stabbing and beating 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, their classmate at a job training facility in Knoxville, in 1995.
The case garnered widespread attention at the time – in part because a pentagram that was carved on Slemmer’s body and other elements of the crime stoked fears of Satan worship during the “satanic panic” of the 1980s and 1990s.
Execution witnesses had already gathered at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville when the order came down at around 9am CDT.
As the execution date drew near, it renewed debate over the death penalty for young offenders.
Pike does not deny committing the killing, but her supporters argue the state should consider Pike’s age at the time, mental illness and a history of severe sexual abuse that included being raped from the time she was a toddler.
Her lawyers also pointed to evidence that Pike's mother drank heavily during pregnancy, contributing to faulty brain development that made it difficult for their client to control her impulses as a young person.
Assistant Federal Defender Stephen Ferrell said Pike’s death sentence is an outlier because other 18-year-olds sentenced to death in Tennessee have had their sentences vacated.

The 1995 killing rocked the city of Knoxville. Prosecutors said Pike – fearing Slemmer was trying to steal her boyfriend – lured her to a wooded area on January 12, 1995. Ukraine unveils new Mavic alternative, but Chinese dependence persists
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
16:02:11 UTC
01:02:11 KST

Ukrainian drone maker Vyriy Industries unveiled its new Slavic reconnaissance drone this week, pitching the aircraft as an alternative to Chinese commercial drones amid domestic efforts to reduce dependence on Chinese technology.
Chinese-made DJI Mavic drones were used by Ukrainian forces years before Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion and have since become commonplace on both sides of the front, both for reconnaissance and dropping explosives. They combine relatively low cost, straightforward controls, and stabilized cameras, letting troops spot infantry, adjust artillery, and direct attacks.
Domestic production of Mavic drone alternatives is especially pressing for Ukrainian security as China’s export restrictions theoretically prohibit shipments of otherwise uncontrolled drones when exporters know, or should know, they are intended for military use.
But domestic production is unlikely to fully eliminate Chinese dependence, as developing drones domestically still involves securing some components in China.
According to Vyriy, the Slavic drone has a tactical operating range of up to 30 kilometers, approximately twice that of a Mavic drone. The company says the greater range is key to allowing reconnaissance crews to operate farther from the line of contact.
"The kill zone has expanded, while the tactical range of available commercial drones remains limited," Vyriy founder and CEO Oleksiy Babenko said in the release.
read also
Vyriy says that pilots familiar with Mavic controls will be able to retrain on the Slavic drone in less than a day. The drone’s controller also supports Ukraine’s Delta battlefield management system and Kropyva tactical software.
While the company said it had completed initial combat testing with seven Ukrainian military units and was preparing to expand production, the announcement did not disclose a price or a production target, making it difficult to assess whether Slavic could replace commercial drones at scale.

Bulgaria to Adopt New Regional Planning Map in 2027, with Sofia as Separate Region
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
16:01:35 UTC
01:01:35 KST

Bulgaria to Test BG-ALERT Emergency System Nationwide Today (October 1)
A national test of Bulgaria’s BG-ALERT emergency notification system will be carried out on October 1, from 11:00 to 11:30 a.
Bulgaria will introduce a new regional division for statistical purposes and regional planning from January 1, 2027. Under a proposal by the Ministry of Regional Development and Public Works, the country’s current six planning regions will be reorganized into four, with the Sofia Municipality forming a separate capital region.
The changes are linked to the new European NUTS classification, which will take effect in 2027. The system determines how territories are grouped for statistical purposes and allows regional data to be compared across EU member states.
Importantly, the new regional structure will not change Bulgaria’s administrative map. No districts or municipalities will be created or abolished, and their administrative boundaries will remain unchanged. The change concerns only the way districts are grouped into larger areas for statistical and planning purposes.
The four new planning regions will be:
The new structure will replace the current Northwest, North Central, Northeast, Southeast, South Central and Southwest planning regions.
There will also be a change at the highest statistical level, NUTS 1.
Currently, Bulgaria is divided into two NUTS 1 regions: Northern and Southeastern Bulgaria, and Southwestern and South Central Bulgaria.
From January 1, 2027, the two regions will be merged into a single NUTS 1 region covering the entire country.
The creation of a separate Capital Region will also bring a different approach to strategic planning.
Integrated Territorial Strategies for Development will be prepared for the Northern, Eastern and Southern regions. For the Capital Region, an Integrated Development Plan will be prepared, serving the functions of an Integrated Territorial Strategy.
The Regional Development Councils will also be reorganized. Instead of the current six councils, there will be four.
According to the Ministry of Regional Development and Public Works, the aim is to align Bulgarian legislation with the new European NUTS classification and adapt the country’s strategic planning system to the new regional structure.
The draft legislation envisages the changes taking effect on January 1, 2027.

A father’s scent helps babies synchronize their brains with new adults
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
16:00:37 UTC
01:00:37 KST

The scent of a father can help babies synchronize their brain activity with unfamiliar adults and encourage more energetic social play. By simply smelling their father’s body odor, infants essentially invoke his presence, allowing them to form stronger neural connections with strangers. These findings were published in the journal Science Advances.
When two people interact socially, their brain waves often align or pulse in harmony. This mechanism, known as interbrain synchrony, helps infants tune their developing brains to their social environment. It allows caregivers to provide sensory inputs that guide the maturation of the child’s social brain.
Past research has shown that maternal body odors can calm infants and increase their neural synchrony with unfamiliar adults. Maternal scents act as an evolutionary signal of safety, helping infants orient toward faces and reducing their neural responses to fearful faces.
However, the impact of a father’s scent on infant brain development has remained largely unexplored. Paternal interactions typically involve different behavioral rhythms than maternal care. Fathers often engage in more high-energy play, which stimulates positive arousal and encourages infants to explore their surroundings. These interactions help children acquire attentive and cognitive skills, opening them up to the broader social world.
Yaara Endevelt-Shapira, a researcher at Reichman University in Israel and the University of Washington, along with Linoy Schwartz and Ruth Feldman, wanted to investigate how infants respond to their father’s smell. They aimed to determine if paternal body odors act as a sensory signal that helps infants build neural connections with people outside their immediate family.
The researchers conducted a small study involving 40 infants, aged five to twelve months, and their biological fathers. To collect the scent, fathers wore a 100 percent cotton t-shirt for two consecutive nights. They were instructed to avoid scented soaps, shampoos, and deodorants, and to refrain from eating foods that heavily alter body odor.
During the laboratory experiment, the researchers used dual-electroencephalography (EEG) to measure the brain waves of both the infants and the adults simultaneously. EEG is a non-invasive method that uses small sensors placed on the scalp to detect electrical activity in the brain. Connecting both participants to the same amplifier guaranteed that the neural recordings were synchronized down to the millisecond.
First, the researchers compared the infants interacting with their own fathers against interactions with an unfamiliar male experimenter. No toys or physical contact were allowed during these three-minute sessions.
The infants displayed higher interbrain synchrony with their own fathers than with the stranger. This synchronization occurred specifically in the alpha frequency band, a type of brain wave that develops during the second half of the first year of life. In infants, alpha oscillations are associated with attention regulation, working memory, and visual processing.
The neural connection linked the father’s left central brain region, which handles sensorimotor processing and skill execution, with the infant’s right temporal region. The right temporal cortex is a core area for processing social information, including biological motion detection and attention.
Next, the researchers tested how the father’s scent altered the infant’s interaction with the unfamiliar male. The infants engaged in two sequential interactions with the stranger. In one session, the t-shirt carrying the father’s body odor was placed near the infant. In the other session, a blank, unworn t-shirt was used as a control.
When the father’s scent was present, the neural synchrony between the infant and the stranger increased. The alignment in the alpha frequency band matched the pattern observed when the infants interacted with their actual fathers. When comparing the neural coupling during the odor condition to the synchrony shared between the infant and their real father, the differences were not statistically significant.
The researchers also analyzed video recordings of the interactions to look for behavioral changes. During the sessions with the stranger, the presence of the father’s scent elevated the infant’s positive arousal. This was measured by instances of smiling, laughing, cooing, and changes in posture such as leaning forward or backward.
While overall visual attention and feelings of safety did not increase universally among the infants, the researchers noticed a correlational trend. Infants who looked more at the stranger’s face and displayed more engagement behaviors experienced a larger boost in neural synchrony.
The researchers also surveyed the fathers about their routine involvement in childcare at home. Infants of fathers who reported higher levels of daily involvement showed a more pronounced increase in neural synchrony when exposed to the paternal odor.
Caregiving behaviors are highly variable and do not strictly align with biological sex. Differences observed between this study on fathers and previous research on mothers might reflect individual parenting styles, parental mental states, or varying levels of childcare involvement.
The infants’ ages spanned a period when alpha brain waves are still maturing. This age-related developmental variation could influence the observed neural patterns. Future studies focusing on a narrower age range could clarify how this specific brain rhythm matures over the first year of life.
The experimental design compared the father’s scent to a blank shirt. This leaves open the possibility that infants were reacting to a general human scent rather than their specific father’s odor, though the stranger’s own scent was present during both conditions.
Additionally, the continuous presence of the scent could lead to olfactory habituation, where the infant stops noticing the smell over time. While the researchers found no neural or behavioral differences between the first and second minutes of the interaction, they acknowledge that capturing dynamic changes in brain activity might require more precise odor delivery methods in the future.
Future research could measure the emotional state of the fathers during the odor collection period, as stress or mood might alter the chemical composition of the scent. Investigating populations with developmental differences, such as infants with a higher likelihood of autism, could reveal whether socially relevant scents might assist in building interpersonal neural connections.
The study, “Scent of a father: Paternal body odors boost interbrain synchrony,” was authored by Yaara Endevelt-Shapira, Linoy Schwartz, and Ruth Feldman.
